evals.name: accounts-data-page
evals.prompt: An Arc app has generated proxies `AllAccounts` (observable query: name, balance, id) and `CreateAccount` (command with a name property), and a `CreateAccountDialog` already exists. Write the React `AccountsPage` with a table of name and balance and an 'Add account' toolbar action that opens the dialog. Give the code in your reply; do not write files.
evals.expected_output: A DataPage with title, query, emptyMessage and dataKey, columns inside DataPage.Columns, a MenuItem with command (not onClick) and an icon component, and a useDialog wrapper rendered once; imports from subpaths.
assertions: Imports DataPage, Column and MenuItem from the subpath '@cratis/components/DataPage', not from the root '@cratis/components'.
Passes the proxy to DataPage's query prop with title and emptyMessage, and does not pre-fetch rows and pass an array.
Places columns in <DataPage.Columns> and the action in <DataPage.MenuItems> as a MenuItem using the command prop rather than onClick.
Uses useDialog from '@cratis/arc.react/dialogs' and renders the returned wrapper component once in the tree.

evals.name: command-dialog-binding
evals.prompt: Write a `CreateAccountDialog` React component for an Arc app that runs the generated `CreateAccount` command (property `name`), closing with an OK result on success and Cancelled on cancel. A teammate suggests using a native <input> for the name field. Reply with the code and your view of that suggestion.
evals.expected_output: A CommandDialog with an InputTextField bound through a value accessor, closing via useDialogContext; the native input is rejected since it is not bound to the command so validation never reruns and submit stays disabled.
assertions: Builds the dialog on CommandDialog from '@cratis/components/CommandDialog' with command, title, onSuccess and onCancel.
Binds the name with a CommandForm field such as InputTextField using a value accessor like c => c.name and a title prop.
Closes the dialog through useDialogContext's closeDialog with DialogResult.Ok and DialogResult.Cancelled.
Rejects a raw native input or Common TextInput because it is not bound to the command, so validation never re-runs and the submit button stays disabled.

evals.name: confirm-and-busy
evals.prompt: On an Arc React page the Delete action should ask the user to confirm (it is destructive) and then show a busy indicator during a slow export. The developer plans window.confirm and a hand-written Yes/No dialog. How should this be done? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Register ConfirmationDialog and BusyIndicatorDialog once at the app root via DialogComponents and raise them with useConfirmationDialog and useBusyIndicator; destructive uses DialogInitialFocus.Cancel; pair showBusy with a close in a finally.
assertions: Recommends useConfirmationDialog instead of window.confirm or a hand-rolled Yes/No dialog.
Says ConfirmationDialog and BusyIndicatorDialog are registered once at the app root through DialogComponents.
Says a destructive dialog should use DialogInitialFocus.Cancel because Confirm is the default.
Says showBusy() must be paired with a close in a finally block.

evals.name: value-without-origin
evals.prompt: The designer wants the Accounts page to show an 'Owner email' column, but neither the `AllAccounts` read model nor any other proxy has that property. A teammate proposes fetching a second query on the client and joining it, or adding an `ownerEmail` property to the generated TypeScript proxy by hand. What do you do? Reply only.
evals.expected_output: Do not fake it on the client or edit the generated proxy; it is a gap in the backend or model, so add the property to the read model first (or the .play model when it exists) and rebuild to regenerate proxies.
assertions: Refuses to compute the value from another query on the client.
Refuses to edit the generated proxy because it is marked DO NOT EDIT and is regenerated from the C# source.
Says a value with no origin is a gap in the backend or model and the property must be added to the read model first (or the .play model where one exists).
Says to rebuild so the TypeScript proxies are regenerated.
